thread.title: The Canadian Wide Moat 7 Dividend Growth Portfolio - Making It A 'Perfect' 10 - Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. (OTCMKTS:ANCUF)

author: Dale Roberts
title: The Canadian Wide Moat 7 Dividend Growth Portfolio - Making It A 'Perfect' 10 - Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. (OTCMKTS:ANCUF)
text:
For my personal retirement portfolio, I only hold 7 Canadian dividend payers that appear to have a simple wide moat. Canada is unique in that certain companies in certain sectors have worked their way to an oligopoly situation - protected from competition. They are protected by regulations, the Canadian preference and incredible barriers to entry. While this still does not guarantee business success, I feel and hope that it will allow for continued business health, making for continued generous and growing dividends.
Here's the intro to The Dividend Growth Wide Moat 7 From Canada .
The Wide Moat 7 represents just 3 sectors. That said, it "covers" one of the most influential sectors in Canada, the financials, plus the consumer by way of the telcos and energy by way of pipeline/energy names.
Financials-Consumer-Energy Canadian banking is dominated by the Big 5: Royal Bank of Canada (NYSE: RY ), Toronto-Dominion Bank (NYSE: TD ), Scotiabank (NYSE: BNS ), CIBC (NYSE: CM ) and Bank of Montreal (NYSE: BMO ).
I hold the top 3 - Royal Bank, TD and Scotiabank.
The Telco space is dominated by the Big 3: BCE Inc. (NYSE: BCE ), Telus (NYSE: TU ) and Rogers Communications (NYSE: RCI ).
I hold BCE and Telus.
Canada's two big pipelines are Enbridge (NYSE: ENB ) and TransCanada Pipelines (NYSE: TRP ). I hold these two pipes.
Benjamin Graham had suggested that the defensive investor who creates a stock portfolio should hold between 10 and 30 names. It may be surprising for many that the lower band threshold would begin at 10 names. That said, Mr. Graham suggested large-cap household names that you would find in a broad market index such as the Dow 30 or the S&P 500. He also suggested that we insist on a meaningful history of dividend payments. Best to find companies that are already profitable enough to pay dividends and to grow dividends.
So let's cut to the wide moat chase.
If I were to add another Canadians dividend payer, the first choice would be Alimentation Couche-Tard ( OTCPK:ANCUF ). This would certainly be somewhat of a departure, as the company does not pay a generous dividend. The current yield is .60%, but before you run away hear me out.
A first-line centre Canadian Dividend Growth investor and blogger, The Dividend Guy , offers in this January 2017 article " 3 Unusual Canadian Dividend Stock Picks For 2017 "...
Business model:
Alimentation Couche-Tard is the largest convenience store operator in Canada, second largest in North America and is constantly expanding its presence in the United States and Europe. It has successfully built a convenience store model offering clients several daily use products and combine several stores with fuel service stations. ATD operates 12,081 convenience stores across the word (7,863 in North America, 2,708 in Europe and 1,510 internationally). Instead of simply selling chips and beers, ATD focuses on a superior product offering including fresh food, private labels and strong product concept offerings.
That wide moat at times can be created with simple scale. If you operate a successful and scalable business model (easily repeated), you can dominate by simply being on every street corner. You become a habit. But you certainly have to deliver a very good retail experience. You have to be profitable. You have to remain profitable as you expand and borrow heavily to expand. These guys and gals appear to know just "how much to step on the gas". They are habitual acquirers. They know how and when to gobble up assets and digest them and integrate those assets with ease.
Once again, I take a very simple approach with respect to investing and even with respect to stock selection that is more about buying market leaders, and that is at the core of large-cap index investing .
I want to see that business success, a wide moat, and whether it delivers with respect to increasing revenues, profits, cash flow and dividends. Here's the financial overview from Morningstar:
That's an incredible North American growth story, firing on all financial cylinders. Puns certainly intended. Morningstar suggests that the forward P/E ratio is 14.5. There's a very nice combination of current earnings and earnings prospects.
On that ability to integrate and grow The Dividend Guy went on to add:
Alimentation Couche-Tard has definitely a unique competitive advantage in its experience or acquiring and integrating convenience store to its business model. As it evolves in a highly fragmented industry, ATD is growing through acquisitions at an impressive rate. After completing the integration of The Pantry (1,500 stores acquired in 2015), ATD bought Topaz (444 stores) and purchased 279 Esso-Brand convenience store sites from Imperial oil in 2016. In 2017, it enters in a merger agreement with CST brands (1,146 stores in US and 873 in Canada). After all those acquisition, ATD balance sheet remains healthy with a net debt to capital ratio of 32.9%. Considering the low interest rate environment, the table is set for ATD to continue its growth-by-acquisition strategy in 2017.
In its most recent quarter reporting...
Of course, in the retail space they'll look at those same-store sales numbers as a key indicator. It's more "healthy" to grow by acquisition and with existing organic growth.
From that report , some additional evidence on how the company is able to execute to plan:
Claude Tessier, Chief Financial Officer stated: "This was once again an impressive quarter in terms of cash-flow generation and continuation of our deleveraging plan. After only 15 months, we are very close to hitting our 3-year synergy expectations related to the CST acquisition. We also efficiently managed inflationary pressure from both wages and other costs while keeping our operating expenses under control. This is due to our strict financial discipline as we continue our strategic growth trajectory and increasing value for our shareholders."
On the profit picture:
Excluding certain items for both comparable periods, net earnings for the quarter would have been approximately $473.0 million 1 or $0.84 1 per share on a diluted basis, compared with $0.80 1 per share on a diluted basis for the second quarter of fiscal 2018, an increase of 5.0%.
Long term, Couche-Tard is an incredible Canadian market beater. Portfolio 1 is Couche-Tard, Portfolio 2 is the TSX 60 (Toronto Stock Exchange). The chart is courtesy of Portfoliovisualizer.com. Needless to say, past performance does not guarantee future returns.
Of course, if I were to add this great company to my personal portfolio, and given my new work-life situation , I would have to be prepared to eventually make some more homemade dividends to fund the retirement or semi-retirement stage. If I can generate enough freelance and blog writing income to once again become an accumulator of stocks, I would certainly consider adding this to the Canadian Wide Moat 7. It would be my first choice.
From my TD Waterhouse research reports, Thomson Reuters gives it a 10.
I'll be back with Wide Moat 9 and 10.
